notes: §1985:IV.6.1.3.1 prints each optional Identification Division paragraph header with its period, '[ AUTHOR. [ comment-entry ] ... ]', and §1985:IV.2.1.6 gives the separator period 'the status of a required word'. Paragraph order, repetition, the AS phrase, the ID DIVISION abbreviation, an unknown paragraph and a missing period after PROGRAM-ID or the division header were already refused; the period of a comment-entry paragraph header was written by the logical conversion whatever the source held, and is now asked of the source in fixed form (kb/Work PB5168, COBOL7166); free form keeps D-CE1's optional period.

next.reason: 1985: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. program-identification-entry, then optional AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED and SECURITY paragraphs of comment-entries. §2023:11.2.1 has "[ IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. ]" (header optional) followed by one id paragraph and [ options-paragraph ], and §2023:10.6.1 restates the same for a program-definition; §2023:11.10.2 keeps PROGRAM-ID. program-name-1. No 2023 rule carries AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED or SECURITY (the paragraph names do not occur in the 2023 text), so a 1985 program using them is refused under 2023, while a program without the header is newly accepted. Both directions are compile-time.
